title: Counting powerful products of consecutive integers
summary: #{n <= x : n, n+1 powerful} << x^(1/4+eps); for each fixed k >= 3, #{n <= x : (n+1)...(n+k) powerful} << x^(77/320+eps); uniformly over all widths k >= 3, << x^(77/320+eps).
grade_note: Lean theorems with standard axioms only; six results from the literature enter the statements as named premises. Every paper-owned step is proved in Lean.

claims.label: thm:k2
claims.statement: For every eps > 0, #{n <= x : n and n+1 are powerful} << x^(1/4+eps).

claims.label: thm:k3
claims.statement: For each fixed k >= 3 and eps > 0, #{n <= x : (n+1)...(n+k) powerful} << x^(77/320+eps); the central subcount (squarefree cube parts of n+1, n+2, n+3 between (n+3)^(19/100) and (n+3)^(21/100)) is << x^(38059/160000+eps).

claims.label: thm:uniform
claims.statement: For every eps > 0, #{n <= x : P(n,k) powerful for some k >= 3} << x^(77/320+eps); with k >= 2 allowed, << x^(1/4+eps); non-powerful members of intervals with powerful product up to x: << x^(77/320+eps).

claims.label: prop:interval
claims.statement: Per-interval count of the determinant method.

claims.label: thm:Bred
claims.statement: The reduced per-box bound x^(max(m, Bred(a,b))+eps).

claims.label: prop:interval-uniform
claims.statement: The per-interval count with an implied constant independent of the shift 1 <= |h| <= x^(delta/4), for c <= 1/10, delta <= 1/100 and coprime solutions.

claims.label: lem:uniformwindows
claims.statement: Uniform primitive windows: the reduced per-box bound uniformly in the shift 1 <= |h| <= x^(delta/4).

claims.label: reuss-window-convention
claims.statement: Reuss's open-endpoint windows cover the closed-endpoint windows of the proof.

claims.label: supporting
claims.paper_ref: Lemmas 2.1-2.3, 5.1, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4, 6.5, 8.1; Propositions 7.1, 7.2; transport in the proof of Theorem 1.3
claims.statement: Supporting declarations cited in Appendix A of the paper.

hypotheses.name: Stewart's Thue bound
hypotheses.source: C. L. Stewart, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 4 (1991), Theorem 1 (p. 795) and its consequence on p. 796
hypotheses.lean_form: binary forms of degree q >= 3, content one, squarefree over Q: at most 2800 q^(1+omega(|m|)) primitive solutions
hypotheses.comparison: Theorem 1 needs only content one and nonzero discriminant (reducible forms included) and counts coprime pairs; p. 796 gives the bound with g = |m|.

hypotheses.name: Castryck-Cluckers-Dittmann-Nguyen bound for integral points on affine curves
hypotheses.lean_form: N = 12; every prime ideal of Q[x_1..x_12] with one-dimensional quotient, degree read from the Hilbert polynomial
hypotheses.compared_against: arXiv text, including Corollary 4.1.4 and Remark 4.1.5
hypotheses.comparison: Covers curves irreducible over Q but not geometrically irreducible via Corollary 4.1.4 and Remark 4.1.5.

hypotheses.name: Gelfond's height inequality
hypotheses.source: Bombieri-Gubler, Heights in Diophantine Geometry, Lemma 1.6.11
hypotheses.lean_form: H(G) <= exp(c_n deg F) H(F) for G | F
hypotheses.comparison: The 2^d bound, d the sum of the partial degrees (d <= n deg F), gives the Lean form with c_n = n log 2.

hypotheses.name: Reuss's window bound
hypotheses.source: T. Reuss, arXiv:1212.3150v2, Theorem 1 with k = 3, l = 2, h = 1
hypotheses.lean_form: windows with D, E >= x^c for each fixed c > 0, comparability constants 1/20 and 20, Reuss's open-endpoint convention
hypotheses.comparison: Used only on windows with both cube-part scales at least a fixed power of x.

hypotheses.name: Heath-Brown's Theorem 15
hypotheses.source: D. R. Heath-Brown, Counting rational points on algebraic varieties, LNM 1891 (2006), Theorem 15 with n = 2; author's manuscript of the lecture notes (Oxford Mathematical Institute eprint 676), Lecture 2, Section 2.6, Theorem 15
hypotheses.lean_form: absolutely irreducible F, complex auxiliary polynomials not divisible by F, factor log(2||F||)
hypotheses.compared_against: the author's manuscript (eprint 676, compiled 2008), and Reuss's thesis Theorem 2
hypotheses.comparison: Source: F in Z[x1,x2] absolutely irreducible of total degree d, B_i >= 1; integer auxiliary polynomials coprime to F, degrees at most D(d, eps), number << T^eps exp(log B1 log B2 / log T) log||F||, ||F|| the largest coefficient modulus. The Lean form needs d >= 2 and B_i >= 2, accepts complex auxiliary polynomials not divisible by F (implied by integer ones coprime to F), and uses log(2||F||) >= log||F||: a weakening. For ||F|| = 1 the source's factor log||F|| vanishes, so the theorem must be read with a factor of at least 1 (for example max(1, log||F||)); under that reading the Lean form is an instance of it.
hypotheses.open: The published LNM text itself was not compared; the author's manuscript was. The exponent 2n-3 of the log factor in the source looks inconsistent with its proof sketch (which suggests 2n-1); the Lean form at n = 2 is unaffected, by an argument of the AI reviewer that is not in the source.

hypotheses.name: Tao's Lemma 3.1
hypotheses.lean_form: for large N, 3 <= k < N and P(N,k) powerful give k <= exp((log N)^(7/10))
hypotheses.comparison: Used only for Theorem 1.3. No explicit value of N_0 is given in the source.
